books.section: A. Farmers and the Populist Party
The Silver Issue and the Populist Movement

primary_sources: Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper, 'The People's Party Convention - Delegates Who Were Not In It,' 1892

stimulus.text: Political cartoon, Frank Leslie’s Illustrated Newspaper, 1892, “The People’s Party Convention—Delegates Who Were Not In It.” At the top left, a group is labeled “A Mixed Delegation.” At the right, a tall figure with his back turned is labeled “Farmers Alliance.” In the center, two men shake hands under the label “Lobby Debate.” In the foreground, a man sleeps on the floor, captioned “Away from the Excitement.”
stimulus.source_note: Frank Leslie’s Illustrated Newspaper, 1892, “The People’s Party Convention—Delegates Who Were Not In It.” Public domain: cartoon published 1892 (pre-1930); Library of Congress, LCCN2004677367. Labels checked against the image.

stem: What does the sleeping man captioned 'Away from the Excitement' suggest?

options.text: The established parties first paid the new party no attention
The People's Party had already won the presidency by 1892
options.misconception: The Populists never won the presidency; Weaver finished third in 1892.

options.text: Farmers were too tired to care about politics at all
options.misconception: Farmers built the Alliance and the party; the sleeper mocks the old parties, not farmers.

options.text: The convention lasted so long that all its delegates fell asleep
options.misconception: The sleeper is one of those 'not in it,' not a tired delegate.

rationales.A: A man asleep through the excitement shows the old parties ignoring the event.
rationales.B: Weaver won 22 electoral votes in 1892, not the presidency.
rationales.C: The farmers organized the convention; the sleeper stands for someone else.
rationales.D: The title says he was not in the convention at all.
rationales.general:
Ask who the sleeper stands for.
1. The man sleeps in the foreground, captioned 'Away from the Excitement.'
2. He is one of the 'delegates who were not in it.'
3. Sleeping through an event means paying it no mind.
4. Background from the books: the major parties first dismissed the Populists as a passing protest.
Remember: a sleeper in a cartoon stands for someone ignoring the action.
